chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, by a chain mentioning from Al-Harith Al-Hamadani who said:

I conversed with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), so I said, 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! A need has presented itself to me.' He said: 'So you view me as a rightful one for it?' I said, 'Yes, O Amir al-Mu'minin!' He said: 'May Allah recompense you goodly from me.' Then he arose to the lantern, so he extinguished it and sat down, then said: 'But rather, I extinguished the lantern perhaps I would see the humiliation of your need in your face, so speak, for I heard Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: The needs are an entrustment from Allah in the chests of the servants, so the one who conceals it, a worship would be Written for him, and the one who exposes it, it would be a right upon the one who hears it that he assists him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of concealing a person's need in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) extinguishes the lantern to conceal the petitioner's face, demonstrating the high Shia ethical value of preserving dignity (khusūʿ) during acts of charity. This act illustrates the concept of 'ḥawāʾij' (needs) as divine trusts, where secrecy in giving is elevated to the status of worship, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition cited by the Imam. The narration underscores the social obligation of the listener to assist if the need is revealed, balancing privacy with communal responsibility.
